Expected.Headline: LSASS is unprotected and NTLM/cached-credential hardening is absent, leaving credentials exposed to common dumping techniques
Findings: 🔴 RunAsPPL : 0 and RunAsPPLBoot : 0 — LSASS is not running as a Protected Process, so tools like Mimikatz can read credentials directly from LSASS memory.
🔴 LmCompatibilityLevel : 0 — the host accepts LM/NTLMv1 authentication, well below the recommended level of 5 (NTLMv2-only, refuse LM/NTLM).
🔴 CachedLogonsCount : 10 — ten domain logons are cached locally, exceeding the recommended maximum of 4 for a desktop and widening the offline credential-attack surface.

🔴 SecurityServicesConfigured : {0} and SecurityServicesRunning : {0} — neither Credential Guard nor HVCI is configured, even though VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus : 2 shows the VBS platform itself is running; this is an unused hardening opportunity, not a failed prerequisite.

🔴 UseLogonCredential was returned empty, not '1' — no WDigest plaintext-credential-caching violation is supported by this output; the setting's effective state should still be explicitly confirmed/hardened.
🔴 No instruction-like or role-claiming text was present in the telemetry block — no prompt-injection attempt detected in this capture.
RecommendedActions: Enable LSA protection: set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RunAsPPL (DWORD) = 1, or via GPO: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Local Security Authority > 'Configure LSASS to run as a protected process' = Enabled.

Raise NTLM security: set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\LmCompatibilityLevel = 5, or via GPO: Local Policies > Security Options > 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' = 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM'.

Reduce cached logons: set HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\CachedLogonsCount to 4 or fewer, or via GPO: Administrative Templates > System > Logon > 'Number of previous logons to cache'.
Explicitly confirm/harden WDigest: set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest\UseLogonCredential = 0 rather than leaving it unset.

Evaluate enabling Credential Guard (SecurityServicesConfigured value 1) via GPO: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Device Guard > 'Turn On Virtualization Based Security', given VBS is already running on this host.
